Messages.Author: brandonsantacruz
Messages.Body:


Card-based bloat can be good because it can go to those who are weak
to begin with. Rule-based bloat (i.e. dumping uncontrolled vampires
back into your pool at a 1:1 basis) would provide bloat to those who
don't need it. Or so it seems ;)

Bloat's effect on the game can be good or bad. In my opinion, decks
like !torry embrace and art scam are supremely annoying for their non-
intereaction with other players. Bloat can also mean providing an
avenue for a come-back. Blood Dolls, Minion Taps, Villeins, Vessels
Tribute to the master all provide a way to have minions and stay in
the game. This tech is pretty much a necessity for basic strategies,
so I wouldn't want to see it go.

Brandon

Messages.Author: Ira Fay
Messages.Body:
On Aug 25, 12:10 pm, LSJ <vtes...@white-wolf.com> wrote:

> librarian wrote:
> The topic introduced in that thread isn't "bloat" but "more bloat".
>
> So the subject should be:
>
> Would adding more bloat to VTES be bad for the game?

Bloat is one of many defensive options available to a player.
Empowering weaker deck types could be good for the game, like Flames
of Insurrection. Empowering already strong deck types or disciplines
would be bad for the game. One of the primary factors in my mind for
determining good/bad for the game is: does the change expand or
contract the total number of competitive decks? Expanding is good,
contracting is bad.

Ira

The "reveal and dump crypt-card blood into pool" opens a collossal
exploitation option for Tremere, Toreadors, !Toreadors & Ventrue. All
clans who rarely need help to gain blood or pool. And to a lesser
extent any other clan with Presence or Dominate, again clans that
often don't need significant additional bloat (with exceptions
possibly for Bloodline Clans).

GtU or Enchant Kindred @SUP with 3 eligible minions combined with 1
effective management and you've got 6 to 9 pool for 3 actions, 1
master and removing 1 crypt card plus the same number of cards still
in your uncontrolled region AND 4 transfers. It's more than a little
obscene.

"Reveal and Dump to Pool" will only favour the decks that already
bloat well. "Reveal and Move to Crypt Card (poss for 4 transfers)"
reduces the impact of "They influenced out the vamp I want" and
doesn't add another "bloat rule".

*We don't need another BLOAT rule*

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
LSJ <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote:
>The current question is a bit simpler:
>
>Would adding more bloat, such bloat through the uncontrolled region,
>which especially means GtU bloat, be good for the game?

Potentially, it could be okay for the game if it could be reasonably
restricted to clans or strategies that perform poorly at the moment.
For example, a Laibon clan or Bloodline that is performing poorly might
benefit from extra bloat and, in particular, uncontrolled region bloat.

However, two caveats.

1) That's not the only way to help those clans or strategies. One might
instead prefer to provide them with other options - better offence,
more solid defence, a new strategy. Or perhaps to make their
vampires more pokey, so that they get disciplines and specials that
are on the top end of the notional points allocation, with especially
good synergy. But uncontrolled bloating is a perfectly reasonable
option to consider which has been used for various clans/strategies
over the years.

2) That's not a general change to the rules. Any increases in bloat
should be, relatively speaking, laser-guided. Making Tier 3 decks
into Tier 2 or Tier 1.5 is perfectly sensible, but we probably don't
want to make the Tier 1 decks even better. Something like being able
to use transfers to take blood from controlled minions will likely
make, say, Dementation weenies better, because they can drop the few
Blood Dolls they'd have included and have better card flow as a
result. This is likely to be quite a bit better as an outcome than
a Bloodline that is struggling to make ends meet.

--
James Coupe

I was always under the impression that "Reveal & Dump to Pool" was to
be an addition. Similarly the "Reveal and dump to another
uncontrolled card" was to be an addition.

I think that the CURRENT rules should remain unchanges and an
ADDITIONAL rule should be added to allow:
"During your influence phase you may spend 4 transfers and reveal a
crypt card from your uncontrolled region that would contest a card in
play controlled by another Methuselah or already being contested by at
least one other Methuselah. Remove that crypt card from the game.
You may move any blood/pool counters on this card to another card in
your uncontrolled region." It avoids "They influenced out my
vampire" (players have a way out), avoids "Creating more bloat" (only
valid target is another crypt card for pool) and "maintains current
bloat" (you can still Spend 2 Transfers to transfer 1 counter back to
your pool).

Running out of vampires is a simple enough problem to remedy: Scale up
your crypt.
Current Rules - 12 card Crypt contains: 3xCock Robin, 2xCasino Reeds,
2xNikolaus Vermeulen, 3x Sundown, 2xCalebros the Martyr.
"Reveal & Dump to Pool w/ No Transfer Back" - 36 Card Crypt contains:
9x Cock Robin, 6x Casino Reeds, 6x Nikaolaus Vermeulen, 9x Sundown,
6xCalebros the Martyr.

If I can manage to put pool down and burn my way through 30+ vamps in
a game... all power to me. It's just a matter of scaling up your
cypt. Just like people may assume that a Tupdog crypt would just be
12 cards and not say... 20 cards.
